newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - British Energy lifts scepticism.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - British Energy lifts scepticism.

text.p: Britain's nuclear power generator British Energy Plc should boost investor confidence with a slight profit after a strong year when it posts its first annual results since flotation last year on June 4.
"It has seen a very strong first year, sustained high levels of output, and a lot of the initial scepticism has been removed," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.
British Energy is expected to turn in a pre-tax profit between 56 and 67 million stg and has said it aims to pay out a total dividend of 13.7 pence per share.
The company's flotation was fraught with problems as shares, sold at 105 pence to institutions on a partly-paid basis, debuted below that level and failed to tip above it until September.
The second tranche of 98 pence is due to be paid in September.
Temporary closure of two of the company's eight modern power stations just days ahead of the share launch only added to market nervousness over the deeply unpopular sale of nuclear power plants.
But since then, scepticism has waned with strong output helping to improve sentiment, analysts said.
"It has demonstrated its ability to keep the stations running and output was very good last year," the analyst said.
British Energy said total output for the year ending March 1997 was 67.21 Terrawatt hours, up from 61.25 Terrawatt hours a year ago.
A Terrawatt is the largest unit of measurement for electricity sales, representing one billion kilowatt hours.

The company also introduced a programme in October to cut 1,460 jobs in the next three years to achieve savings of 50 million stg a year with a restructuring cost of 100 million fully covered by provisions.
But the company is highly sensitive to fluctuations in prices at the wholesale market for electricity, known as the "pool," and inflation.
"We'd like to see their thinking on pool prices and output prospects this year," the analyst said.
The company will also be pressed to outline its strategy, particularly over its purchase in April of a 12.5 percent stake in combined cycle gas plant operator Humber Power Ltd.
British Energy paid as much as 28 million stg for the stake but analysts said it would have to prove it could add more value than just an investment.
"It seems the Humber deal is just buying shares. Investors can do that. We'd like to see British Energy adding value," the analyst said.
